ground_truth.description: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.root_cause: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test locks 500e18, increases by 500e18 in one tx, and shows reduced bribe rewards compared to separate locks.
ground_truth.fix_description: In `_checkpoint`, overwrite the latest point if timestamps match, else append a new one. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: When create_lock + increase_amount occur in one tx, _checkpoint appends a new point_history entry with identical timestamp (block.timestamp) instead of overwriting the latest point. This causes balanceOfNFT to read stale user_point data, under-calculating voting power for the combined lock amount.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Call create_lock(500e18, duration) then immediately increase_amount(tokenId, 500e18) in same tx. 2. _checkpoint records two points at same ts. 3. balanceOfNFT reads only first point, returning ~half expected votes. 4. Bribe/reward distributions and governance votes use reduced power permanently until next checkpoint.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: In _checkpoint, before writing point_history[_epoch], check if votingBalanceLogicData.point_history[_epoch].ts == block.timestamp; if so overwrite instead of incrementing _epoch.

prediction.overall_explanation: The documented checkpoint timestamp collision bug is present in the code and produces a concrete, exploitable reduction in voting power for multi-deposit transactions without requiring any privileged role.
